cells.label: fact
cells.reason: The passages name competitors Raymond James faces around its affiliation models and advisor recruiting, which is what the sub-question asks.

items.text: Raymond James states it competes directly with national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and faces competition from newer entrants including fintechs, as well as indirect competition for investment assets from insurance companies, real estate firms and hedge funds.
items.quote: We compete directly with other national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers. We face competition from more recent entrants into the market, including fintechs... We also compete indirectly for investment assets with insurance companies, real estate firms, and hedge funds, among others.

items.text: Raymond James says the continued industry-wide trend of financial advisors departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or join existing third-party RIAs some of which are backed by private equity investors, has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.
items.quote: Our PCG business is subject to risks arising from the continued industry-wide trend in which financial advisors are departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs, some of which are backed by private equity investors. This ongoing trend has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.

items.text: Raymond James says many of its competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or less, many compete with the largest check, and many change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.
items.quote: whereas so many of our competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or even less... whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check... whereas many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

items.text: Raymond James names PE-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel competitive dynamic, saying they have been extremely aggressive in paying higher and higher multiples for advisors over the last three years.
items.quote: The dynamic that's relatively novel in the last five years is these PE-backed roll-ups cropping up everywhere. Over the last three years in particular, they've been extremely aggressive in trading and paying at higher and higher multiples.

items.text: Raymond James says it still sees pressure on the existing advisor base from private equity roll-ups, which in the absence of a value proposition compete with big checks.
items.quote: We are still seeing pressure on the existing advisor base, private equity. We always say with the roll-ups, in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks.

items.text: Raymond James says there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.
items.quote: Yeah, there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.

items.text: Raymond James says many competitors that focus on personal relationships and have similar cultures invest only a fraction of what it does in technology, making it hard for them to remain competitive.
items.quote: a lot of our competitors who also are focused on personal relationships, and that have similar cultures, their technology investment, for example, is a fraction of ours. And that's hard to remain in competitive when you can't invest in AI and the tools that you need

items.text: Raymond James says competitors that lack a true differentiated value proposition lead with the highest check.
items.quote: We don't lead with the highest check... In the absence of a true differentiated value proposition, the highest check is all you have.

items.text: Raymond James says advisors are coming to it from a lot of different competitor firms, including wirehouses, regionals and other independents.
items.quote: Advisors are coming from, you know, wires, regionals, other independents.

items.text: Raymond James says private equity has certainly been competitive over the last five years, as well as some of the strategic firms.
items.quote: Private equity has certainly been competitive over the last 5 years as well as some of the strategic firms.

items.text: Raymond James notes it is possible that certain of its competitors will withdraw from the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when they affiliate with a new firm.
items.quote: Participation in the Protocol is voluntary, and it is possible that certain of our competitors will withdraw from it.
